request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: If, after the tenancy has begun, the Landlord and the Tenant agree to end it on a date they both choose, neither of them needs to give a notice of termination.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
Under the Ontario *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (RTA), this clause is enforceable because it simply restates the law regarding mutual agreements to terminate a tenancy. 

Subsection 37(3) of the RTA explicitly states that a notice of termination is not required if a landlord and a tenant have entered into an agreement to terminate a tenancy. Furthermore, subsection 37(4) clarifies that an agreement to terminate is void if it is entered into at the time the tenancy agreement is entered into. Because the clause specifies that the agreement to end the tenancy happens *after* the tenancy has begun, it complies with both subsections and does not conflict with the Act.

Verdict: enforceable
Section: 37
